newsitem.title: USA: U.S. urges Americans to leave Congo Brazzaville.
newsitem.headline: U.S. urges Americans to leave Congo Brazzaville.

text.p: The U.S. State Department on Saturday strongly urged American citizens to leave the Congo Brazzaville because of what it called "the deteriorating security situation" in the capital.

"Shooting and other acts of violence have occurred between elements of the Congolese military and paramilitary groups. Combatants have set up roadblocks in various parts of the city and movement within the city is dangerous," it said in a written statement.
The department also authorised the voluntary departure of dependents of U.S. Embassy personnel from the Central African country.
"A dusk-to-dawn curfew is in place. Ferry service to Kinshasa is inoperable at present. Flights to and from Brazzaville are subject to cancellation or delay on short notice," the statement said.
A group of 44 U.S. citizens on Saturday flew out of Brazzaville, capital of the former French colony, for Kinshasa, the capital of Laurent Kabila's neighbouring Democratic Republic of Congo.

One French soldier was killed and five wounded in Brazzaville after a third day of bloodshed in the capital as rival political and ethnic militias clashed in advance of an election planned for July 27.
